title: Delivery of membrane impermeable molecules to primary mouse T lymphocytes
protocol: Harvest day 3-activated mouse T cells from 24-well plates.
Resuspend semi-adherent mouse T cells with a P-1000 pipette.
Transfer all cultured cells from the same mouse/genotype into one 15 mL conical tube.
Spin down the conical tube at 500× g for 3 min at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
Resuspend cell pellet in 10 mL of RPMI 1640 and spin down again under the same conditions.
Repeat the washing step twice more, totaling three washes to thoroughly clean cells.
After washing, resuspend the cell pellets in a small volume of RPMI 1640 (1 or 2 mL recommended).
Count the number of live cells using an automated cell counter or hemocytometer and exclude dead cells stained with trypan blue.
Use 1 million live cells per sample for all experimental setups described.
Transfer 1 million live cells from different genotypes or samples to a 96-well plate as required by the experiment.
Fill up each well containing cell samples with RPMI 1640 to a final volume of 300 μL.
Rest the cell samples in a tissue culture incubator at 37°C with 5% CO2 for 3 h.
Spin down the cells in the 96-well plate at 500× g for 3 min at 20°C–22°C (room temperature).
Resuspend and wash the cell pellets with 300 μL Ca2+- and Mg2+-free HBSS solution.
Spin down the cells at 500× g for 3 min at 20°C–22°C (room temperature).
Repeat the washing step with Ca2+- and Mg2+-free HBSS three times.
Dilute the SLO stock solution to the optimal concentration using Ca2+- and Mg2+-free HBSS solution.
Add the substance to be delivered intracellularly to the SLO-containing solution.
Warm up the SLO and the supplement solution to 37°C in a water bath.
Resuspend cell samples in the SLO solution with or without the supplement substance after washing cells.
Incubate the resuspended cells in a tissue culture incubator at 37°C with 5% CO2.
Prepare a solution containing biotinylated CD3 and CD28 antibodies in Ca2+- and Mg2+-containing HBSS or RPMI 1640.
Add 5 μg/mL of anti-CD3 antibody to the solution.
Add 2 μg/mL of anti-CD28 antibody to the solution.
Mix the solution thoroughly.
Incubate cells with the prepared solution at 4°C for 30–40 minutes.
Wash cells twice with Ca2+- and Mg2+-containing HBSS or RPMI 1640 by centrifugation at 500× g for 3 min at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
Resuspend the washed cells in 100 μL of solution containing anti-CD3/anti-CD28 antibodies and any supplementary substance.
Incubate resuspended cells at 4°C or on ice to minimize endocytosis.
Warm up the bottom of the 96-well plate in a water bath for 2 min without contaminating samples with water.
Add 5 μl of 20× streptavidin solution into 100 μl per sample and mix well.
Incubate the mixture either in a 37°C water bath or an incubator for 5 minutes to allow crosslinking.
Spin down the cells quickly after crosslinking.
Add 100 μL of 1× cell lysis buffer containing phosphatase and protease inhibitors to every 106 cells for immunoblotting samples.
Coat a chamber slide with poly-D-lysine solution diluted to 50 μg/mL in sterile PBS without Ca2+ and Mg2+.
Incubate the slides at room temperature (20°C–22°C) for 1 hour.
Remove the solution and wash the slides three times with 300 μL of distilled water.
Dry the coated slides uncovered in the laminar hood or store them sealed with parafilm at 4°C until use.
Transfer cell samples to different wells of the chamber slide after step 17 from a previous section.
Spin down the samples at 500× g for 5 minutes to allow cells to adhere to the bottom of the slide.
Warm up the chamber slide in a water bath for 2 minutes.
Gently remove half (50 μL) of the solution in the chamber slide.
Add 50 μL of the 2× streptavidin solution to each well of the chamber slide.
Incubate the chamber slide at 37°C for 5 minutes.
Spin down the chamber slide quickly.
Remove the supernatant carefully.
Add 200 μL of 4% PFA solution to fix the cells.
Fix the cells at room temperature (20°C–22°C) for 10 minutes.
Aspirate the supernatant slowly and carefully without disturbing the cells.
Tilt the slide and aspirate liquid from the edge using a thin western loading tip.
Add PBS slowly along the chamber wall, tilting the slide to distribute the buffer gently without detaching cells.
Wash cells with 250 μL of PBS once in the chamber slide by touching the pipette tip to the wall and discharging the buffer slowly.
Fix the cells again with 250 μL of Tonbo nuclear protein fixation buffer at room temperature for 40–60 minutes.
Aspirate the supernatant after fixing.
Wash the cells once with 250 μL of Tonbo permeabilization buffer slowly and carefully without disturbing the cells.
Prepare 250 μL antibody solution per sample using Tonbo permeabilization buffer.
Add 250 μL of the antibody cocktail to the samples.
Incubate at 4°C for 12–16 hours.
Aspirate the primary antibodies slowly and carefully.
Wash the sample twice with PBS at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
Add 250 μL of secondary antibodies per sample.
Incubate for 1 hour at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
Wash the cells with PBS twice at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
Incubate cell samples with hoechst diluted in PBS for 10 minutes at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
Wash the cells with PBS twice.
Make hoechst stock solution at a concentration of 10 mg/mL and dilute it in PBS at a ratio of 1:500 to 1:2000.
Remove the chamber wall slowly and carefully.
Add 2–3 drops or enough antifade mountant on top of the samples slowly and carefully.
Apply the cover slide carefully.
Take images with immunofluorescent microscopy (ZEISS LSM 880) using a desired setup and magnification.
